 Coram : Rajnish R. Vyas, J.

Date : February 03, 2026
 Judgment :

1. This is an appeal preferred by the claimant challenging the common judgment and award passed by the District Judge-2, Jalna, on 03rd May 2008, by which the compensation was determined for dry land at the rate of  1,000/- per Are.
The appellant's reference 928.FA.460.2019 bearing No.339 of 1997 was also one of the matters which was decided by the common judgment dated 03rd May 2008.

sentences.text: 2. The land of the appellant bearing Gut No.57, admeasuring 4 H 69 R, situated in village Kedarwakadi, was subjected to acquisition for the purpose of a 100-meter plinth of the Nimna Dudhana Project Dam.
The notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act was issued on 20th April 1995, whereas the award was passed on 30 th April 1996, by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
3. While passing the common order dated 03rd May 2008, the Reference Court i.e., the District Judge-2, Jalna, had also decided Land Acquisition Reference No.349 of 1997.

4. According to the Mr. Kakade, the claimant in Land Acquisition Reference No.340 of 1997, taking an exception to the award dated 03rd May 2008, had preferred First Appeal No.1896 of 2021 before this Court, and this Court, vide its order dated 05 th January 2026, allowed the first appeal and awarded rate of  2,400/- per Are.
He has tendered a copy of the aforesaid order dated 05 th January 2026 to this Court, which is taken on record and marked "X" for identification.

He thus submitted that the issue is no more res integra and, in view of the order dated 05th January 2026 passed by this Court in First Appeal No.1896 of 2021, in which compensation for dry land was enhanced at the rate of  2,400/- per Are, the appellant is also entitled for the same on the basis of parity.
6.
Mr. Ram Deshpande, learned counsel appearing for the acquiring body, has fairly submitted that the issue is covered by the aforesaid order and requested that a suitable order be passed.
7. I have gone through the record of the case.

First Appeal No.1896 of 2021, more particularly order dated 05 th January 2026, has resolved the controversy in Land Acquisition Reference No.340 of 1997 and has held that compensation for dry land at the rate of  2,400/- per Are can be granted,
thus, in the present case also since the land owned by the claimant is also a dry land.
8.

Since the issue is already covered by the order dated 05th January 2026 passed in First Appeal No.1896 of 2021, the present appeal is allowed in the following terms :
928.FA.460.2019 ORDER A) The First Appeal is allowed.
B) The appellant shall be awarded enhanced compensation at the rate of  2,400/- per Are.

C) The appellant shall be entitled to the interest under Sections 28 and 34 of the Land Acquisition Act as per the Full Bench Judgment of this Court in the case of State of Maharashtra Vs. Kailash Shiva Rangari1.
D) The appellant shall not be entitled to the interest and the statutory benefits for the delayed period.
